name: Palma Lagoon 42
why: 2019 Lagoon 42 at €269k is a major age/size/price comp; 57hp Yanmars and 4-cabin layout with enough spread versus $380–400k 450s to fund substantial upgrades.
risks: ~4,104h engines; tax not paid; need fleet/phase-out history, saildrives, standing rigging/sails, structural/damage history and current systems inventory.
next_step: Get maintenance/phase-out records, survey, damage history, saildrives/rig/sails and seller flexibility.
notes: NEW PRIORITY: perhaps the strongest 42-ft European value comp found so far.

name: DONNA JUNE
why: 2020 Lagoon 42 already released from charter and in St. Lucia for phase-out/closing; very young platform with twin 45hp Yanmars and strong Caribbean starting location.
risks: ~2,600–2,700h engines; ex-charter; need actual handback scope, saildrives, rig/sails, structural/damage history and off-grid equipment details.
next_step: Get handback/phase-out work list, maintenance file, survey/damage history, saildrives/rig/sails and seller flexibility.
notes: NEW PRIORITY: direct peer to WANDERER; two St. Lucia 2020 Lagoon 42s are listed around $329k.

name: RSB2 Lagoon 42
why: 2018 Lagoon 42 at €260k with ~3,800h engines; extremely competitive headline economics for a 42 and Caribbean location.
risks: Need recent survey, full maintenance history, saildrive/rig/sail history, structural/moisture findings, damage/insurance history and actual liveaboard system spec.
next_step: Get survey, maintenance/damage history, saildrives/rig/sails and seller flexibility; compare hard against Palma 2019 and 2020 St. Lucia boats.
notes: NEW PRIORITY: sub-€300k Lagoon 42 comp; strong enough to challenge much higher-priced 450s.

name: Cristal
why: 2018 450F at a sharply reduced €299k in ideal Bahamas geography; Dream/Navigare confirms its Lagoon 450s received the bulkhead repair, removing one major structural unknown.
risks: Ex-charter since new / listed Fair; standing rigging is ORIGINAL and genset is ~8,000h. Off-grid electrical modernization, rig replacement and generator reserve are meaningful; buyer must commission survey after fleet use ends.
next_step: Keep as a value 450, not a turnkey boat. Wait for Moet/Loumilis follow-up and phase-out timing; for Cristal specifically price a full rig + generator reserve before considering an offer.
notes: Gerry confirms all their Lagoon 450s have had bulkhead repairs; Cristal retains original standing rigging and has ~8,000h genset. This materially lowers its ranking despite the €299k ask.

name: Moet
why: 2018 450F in the BVI with documented Lagoon/VPLP forward-bulkhead reinforcement completed by Navigare BVI in 2023, plus generator-powered A/C and inverter. Available now.
risks: Fresh broker facts materially weaken the turnkey case: about 3,500h engines, about 5,000h generator, original standing rigging and sails, acid batteries and no solar. Ex-charter and listed Fair; saildrives and phase-out condition still need independent survey.
all_in_display: ~€404–434k plus VAT/tax/survey/closing; higher if genset or saildrives need major work
next_step: No further outreach needed now. Treat as a refit platform, not turnkey: obtain phase-out file, saildrive history and actual bulkhead certificate before any offer. Only rises again with meaningful seller flexibility.
notes: 9/3 hard facts: engines about 3,500h; genset about 5,000h; acid batteries; original rig and sails; no solar; available now. The 2023 bulkhead work remains its major positive.

name: Altair
why: Factory-certified preventative bulkhead reinforcement in 2023; 60+ documented maintenance/upgrades since 2024; April 2026 oil tests; scheduled haulout/bottom + saildrive/drivetrain service included.
risks: ~4,086h Yanmars and syndicated spec shows ~13,000h on the 13.5kW Onan generator. Standing rig/sail ages and true off-grid battery/solar setup still unclear; tax not paid.
next_step: Get bulkhead certificate, 60-item work file, oil reports, rig/sails, electrical spec and exact genset health/refit history; test price flexibility.
notes: NEW: strong maintenance story, but 13k-hour genset prevents a turnkey assumption.

name: Total Eclipse
why: Never chartered owner layout with ~2.74kW solar, large LiFePO4 bank, watermaker, washer/dryer, master A/C and 2025 Coppercoat; seller is explicitly motivated and current engine hours are now confirmed around 2,225.
risks: Broker has little documentation available before contract/due diligence; only 2kW portable generator and single-zone A/C. Rig/sail, saildrive and battery history still need documentation. Owner reports no damage/claims/groundings/structural repairs, but this remains unverified.
next_step: YOUR DECISION: whether the motivated seller justifies negotiating a contract subject to document review, walkthrough, haulout/survey and sea trial before spending money to travel. No contract or visit discussion initiated.
notes: Broker confirms ~2,225h actual current engine hours. Boat will haul for hurricane season; seller motivation is time/project driven. Due-diligence records would be obtained from owner during contract period.
